biography.plain_text: Isak Andic was a Turkish-born Spanish billionaire who founded the Barcelona fashion retailer Mango. After moving to Catalonia at fourteen, he began in wholesale and retail before opening Mango in 1984. He remained its controlling shareholder and non-executive chairman as it expanded internationally, retaining those roles until his death in 2024.

long_biography.plain_text:
The enterprise began with embroidered blouses bought from a sailor and resold to Barcelona shops. As orders outgrew a bag, Isak Andic moved through a suitcase, a car boot and warehouse space, then market stalls and multi-brand shops. In 1984 he brought the trading operation together under Mango.

Family ownership was eventually separated from professional management. Andic appointed Toni Ruiz chief executive in 2020 and subsequently granted him a 5% stake, while retaining the other 95% and serving as non-executive chairman. After Andic's death, Ruiz became chairman; Jonathan, Judith and Sarah Andic assumed leadership positions within the family's holding structure.

uncertainties.detail: Mango, Companies House and the Spanish official gazette identify the subject as Isak Andic Ermay, while Forbes and Mango's own page heading use the public name Isak Andic. In Spanish legal-name order, Ermay appears as a second family name rather than a middle name. The saved display name is therefore retained and middle_names is left blank rather than misordering the legal name in a field that cannot represent a second surname cleanly.

Mango and Forbes agree on a 1953 birth, while Companies House narrows it to October 1953. Tertiary English and Spanish biographies disagree between 1 and 20 October, so the month and year are proposed but birth_day remains unresolved. The saved age of 67 on 7 May 2020 would imply an earlier birth and is treated as an imprecise snapshot because first-party sources and the reported age of 71 at death converge on 1953.

Turkey is already saved as birth country.

Forbes expressly labels the fortune self-made and the operating history begins with small-scale clothing sales rather than an inherited Mango business. His brother participated in early ventures, and reliable sources do not provide a complete account of family capital or starting resources. The broader Self-made value is therefore selected; Self-made — independent start is the strongest narrower alternative but does not clear the evidence threshold.
